hints: Look closely at the fatty acid tails in A, B, C and D and count how many kinks or bends you can see in each molecule.
Remember that a kink is caused by a cis C=C double bond (unsaturated tail) and stops tails packing tightly together, so more kinks means more fluidity.
walkthrough:
**Spot what is different about the tails**

Look at the zig-zag tails. A has two perfectly straight tails. B, C and D have bends where there is a double bond (=). Count the bends in each molecule.

A = 0 bends, B = 1 bend, C = 2 bends, D = 4 bends.

**Link double bonds to fluidity**

Straight saturated tails can pack very closely together with strong hydrophobic interactions, so the membrane is more rigid.

A kinked unsaturated tail cannot pack closely. It pushes neighbouring phospholipids apart, making the membrane more fluid and flexible.

**Pick the most unsaturated molecule**

More double bonds means more kinks and less packing, so more fluidity. Molecule D has the most double bonds in both of its tails, so it will disrupt packing the most and contribute most to fluidity.

options.A: Both tails are straight and saturated with no double bonds, so they pack tightly and decrease fluidity, not increase it.
options.B: Only one double bond (one kink) in one tail, so it increases fluidity a little but much less than molecules with more kinks.
options.C: Has two double bonds in total, so more fluid than A and B, but still fewer kinks than D so it packs more closely than D.
options.D: Has four double bonds (two kinks in each tail), so it packs least well and keeps phospholipids furthest apart, giving the greatest fluidity.
